entry.name: Talos electrician conduit and subpanel sample
entry.title: Free sample: electrician installing an outdoor conduit run and subpanel: head-mounted stereo egocentric video + depth, tactile sensor gloves on both hands (24 IMUs, 20 force pads, force in newtons) and 3D hand pose for both hands
entry.venue: Hugging Face dataset (free sample of a commercial dataset)
entry.summary: Three episodes (306 s) of a master electrician strapping PVC conduit, connecting feeder wires in a new subpanel and routing them in the main panel, recorded on 3 November 2026 with Talos gloves on both hands (10 force-sensing-resistor pads and 12 IMUs each, 200 Hz) and a head-mounted Luxonis OAK-D Pro W with stereo-derived depth; wrist positions in the camera come from forearm AprilTags.
entry.hand: Talos glove x 2, worn under red work gloves

sensor.note: 10 force-sensing-resistor pads per hand: F0 thumb pad, F1-F4 index to little fingertips, P0 thenar, P1 hypothenar, P2 distal palm, P3 central palm, P4 index-base palm; conductance (observation.hand.<side>.pads) and estimated newtons (observation.hand.<side>.pad_force) at 30 Hz in the LeRobot frames, 200 Hz raw in the talos/ sidecar.
sensor.range: peak readings in the sample 0.1-23.1 N per pad

scale.text: Sample: 3 episodes, 306 s, 9,180 frames per stream at 30 fps (steps 33-35 of a 38-step, 45-minute job); the full recording is sold separately

entry.access: Hugging Face talosdataworks/electrician-conduit-subpanel-two-hand-tactile-glove-sample, ungated, 2.51 GB (LeRobot v2.1 parquet, AV1 and lossless HEVC depth videos, plus a talos/ folder of raw sensor streams); the full 45-minute job is offered through Datarade or talosdataworks.com/datasets.

gate.note: The three-episode sample is public; the card says the full 38-step dataset is available from Talos Dataworks on Datarade or through talosdataworks.com/datasets and is licensed separately for commercial use. No price is stated.

caveats: Five minutes from one electrician at one residential site; CC BY-NC 4.0 covers the sample only.

Force in newtons comes from bench curves of the right glove's pads, reused for the left glove (P4 uses Interlink's published FSR 400 curve). The card gives hysteresis of 27-52% per pad, repeatability 6.6-28.5% (80.2% on the ring tip) and drift 8.3-14.2% in about 5 min, all above its targets, and says a 2 N reading may be anywhere from about 1 to 3 N.
Right-hand pads F0, F1, F2 and P2 register contact in 0.0% of frames and right P0 carries a steady preload, so most right-hand fingertip touch is missing; left-hand peaks reach 23.1 N (index tip).

Hand pose comes from the glove IMUs on a template skeleton (not fitted MANO parameters), not checked against motion capture; the card expects offsets of up to about 10 degrees. Wrist positions exist only where a forearm tag is seen or bridged: 33% of frames for the left hand, 19% for the right.
Depth was computed after recording from the stereo pair with the projector off; it reaches no nearer than about 0.17 m.
Another sample from the same seller is catalogued as talos_electrician_wirenuts (one right-hand glove, a different job).
